narration: First, reference video frames undergo head extraction, feeding into Depth Net and Pose Net to estimate 3D facial depth and head poses.
Next, flow computed from 3D geometry warps encoded features into canonical space, where a ConvLSTM aggregates them to generate a neutral canonical head.
In the fusion stage, the canonical head is transformed by the target pose alongside the driving and reference video frames.
A central predictor takes all three representations to jointly estimate optical flow fields and attention weight maps.
Features from both branches are encoded, warped with the predicted flow fields, and modulated by their respective attention maps.
Finally, the decoder combines the attention-weighted features to synthesize the photorealistic driving frame.
